text:
natalie: FYI — saw GPU autoscaler failing in us-west-2 this morning. New nodes spin up but fail decrypting node secrets. Provisioning queue backed up (~120 pending).

kevin: omg saw the alerts. Any pattern in the failures? same AZ?

natalie: mostly us-west-2b and 2c. Network team pushed a firewall rule tightened to deny unknown egress on the management subnets overnight. suspect the rule blocked keystore handshake.

rahul: can we get the node agent log?

natalie: paste from `gpu-init-2102`:
```
2025-12-02T00:41:02Z ERROR keystore: client handshake failed: tls: handshake did not complete
2025-12-02T00:41:02Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = upstream connection closed
2025-12-02T00:41:02Z INFO  onboarding: retrying join (attempt=3)
```

kevin: matches blocked outbound TCP to 443 on keystore cluster. Firewall logs show reset from the new deny rule + a Conntrack mismatch when nat gateway was also in path.

security-bot: automated alert CL-SEC-2025-922: detected egress policy change in us-west-2 that affects service keystore.internal.redwood; severity: medium; suggested action: allowlist keystore FQDN for management subnets.

rahul: two quick options: 1) open emergency allow on firewall for `keystore.internal.redwood` from mgmt-subnets (fast), 2) add a temporary IAM condition to let nodes fetch secrets via instance profile (messy), 3) route mgmt-subnet egress through existing approved proxy (preserves audit) but needs route update.

kevin: prefer 3 if we can do <15m. preserves audit chain. Route flip cost = minimal. Option 1 is easier but bypasses inspection.

natalie: downside of 3 — nat/proxy path has a conntrack limit that already occasionally hits during scaleups. If we push all onboarding traffic through it we'll see short spikes. That conntrack issue is on the backlog.

rahul: what about combining 1 + 3: open allow for only the currently provisioning subnet CIDRs for 2h while we route the rest through proxy? Limits blast radius and keeps compliance data for most traffic.

natalie: reasonable. Compliance will want a justification.

ops-bot: runway command issued: apply-route-change mgmt-subnet -> proxy-gw (initiated by kevin). ETA 120s for BGP reconverge.

kevin: route applied. rolling restart of agent watchers in that AZ to reattempt join.

natalie: join success jumped from 55% -> 94% in 10m. decrypt errors dropped to single digits.

rahul: opened security ticket SEC-OPEN-775 with the firewall team to add a scoped host allow for `keystore.internal.redwood` for mgmt-subnets for 2 hours, and escalate conntrack quota bump for the proxy. cc @compliance.

security-bot: note: audit log coverage will be partial if we keep direct allow. request documented exception if >1h.

kevin: cost note: routing via proxy increases per-node onboarding latency by ~120ms and adds ~2% egress billed on proxy flow logs, estimate ~$3/day at current scale. small.

natalie: long-term proposals: A) maintain an explicit managed-egress VPC for onboarding that always hits audited proxy (preferred for compliance), B) add keystore regional anycast endpoint inside each region (needs infra change), C) relax firewall rules with DNS-based allowlist (risky due to DNS poisoning).

rahul: let's schedule an RFC for A and B. For now we keep hybrid: proxy route + 2h scoped allow for the burst CIDRs. owners: kevin (route), natalie (monitor), rahul (ticket & RFC).

natalie: will monitor warm pool and conntrack metrics. will report back in 6h or earlier if we see regressions.

kevin: thanks team. closing the emergency loop for now.

ops-bot: incident followup created: INC-2025-1204 (owner: rahul).
